This would be the cruz of my argument.

 

Medico is screaming (in my mind) in pain because something is "WRONG" with the flow of energy in the area. They have no idea what it is and just now it is something. They come to a perfectly normal looking house.

 

Now, at this point, technically, you might be able to bring Mainstay up on property damages for busting through the door, but there is precendence for forced entry if you believe a crime is being committed, and something causing that sort of energy signature screams "Supervillain up to something really bad"

 

I'll grant, they are civilians not cops, but that's muddying the waters when talking superheroes, and this falls under the same blanket as the events of "The Trial of Baron Blade" did you technically do wrong by breaking a machine that the creator only claimed was going to vaporize the city even if it was incapable of doing so… maybe, but would you want the heroes to stop and go through the proper channels only to find out the machine could actually vaporize a city and they let innocents die?

 

Mainstay busts in and sees a woman, an infernal machine (I'm going to say comic book logic says the machine is clearly dangerous and unhealthy looking) and at best a young girl passed out in the machine, at worst a young girl in obvious agony in the machine. Yes, Idealist did not have any "sentience" but her body was alive meaning it could likely react to pain stimulus.

 

Are you going to take the time and confirm the young child is actually a livnig being and not a mindless clone. No, she's a child and she's in pain and who knows what this "Anit-life" machine is going to end up doing. We know in fact, the machine was going to kill her.

 

So he acted, and it may be a legal mess to sort out in real-life, but in the end the most juries are going to agree that there was every reason to suspect that Mainstal was saving a minimum of two lives with his actions, acting in defense of his friend's life and the life of a young child, and possibly more if the device had been some sort of weapon. He'd get in trouble, but it would be a light sentence, probably a fine and some community service with minimum jail time, since no one died.
